answer: Cross-chain binding at the lotus: each identity must lock collateral on two chains, verified by light-client proofs. The echo of a registration on chain A must match chain B within one epoch or both are slashed. An atlas of addresses lets any verifier trace duplicate proofs. Attacker cost: 2× collateral per identity plus slashing risk. Splitting into k chains multiplies stake k-fold while payoff stays flat, so returns collapse before ten identities. Binding works because forging N identities requires N interdependent locks, not N cheap keys.
